parties:
Mosammat Kazi Shamsunnahar
Vs.
Md. Ramjan Molla and others
full_judgment: 4. Mr. Kazi Abdul Khaleque, the learned advocate for the petitioner submitted that both the courts below committed gross illegality in violating the clear provision of law that the properties transferred through exchange deed was non pre-emptable under section 96(10) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and as such the Miscellaneous Case No. 35 of 1999 was not tenable in law but even then purposely both the courts below violated this aspect of mandatory provision of law that occasioned failure of justice. The aforesaid pre-emption case according to the learned advocate also was hit by principle of estoppels, waiver and acquiescence because the pre-emptor and the sellers being full brothers were the parties in the negotiation of transfer of the suit land to the petitioner which both the courts did not consider. In course of his argument the learned advocate placed before this court the decrees of the courts below with short background of the case land that the seller opposite party No. 2 Md. Khalilur Rahman full brother of Md. Ramzan Molla, the pre-emptor who sold secretly the suit land to the petitioner purchaser Mosammat Kazi Shamsunnahar by Saf Kabala deed dated 09.06.1998 but the said kabala was shown as an exchange deed to avoid the pre-emption against the same. The petitioner opposite party No. 1 being the co-sharer of the khatian of the suit land is entitled to pre-empt the said suit land. Hence he has filed this miscellaneous case. He again submitted that huge amount the purchaser petitioner spent in the suit land for establishment of paltry firm, construction of large tin-sheet house, installation of the electricity with other materials and presently the value of the suit land with the aforesaid establishment would be minimum ten times higher then the original price of the suit land and if the paltry firm would be abolished then a large number of workers would go for unemployment. This humanitarian side was not considered by the courts below applying their judicial mind. He finally submitted that the courts below for the reasons known to them abruptly considered the exchange deed as kabala that was a commission of error of law occasioned failure of justice. In support of his contention he cited the decisions in the cases of Birendra Nath Kar -Vs- Abdul Mannan Kazi and others, reported in 10 BLC (AD)-157, Mozibar Rahman Molla and another -Vs- Md. Rehazuddin and others, reported in 8 BLC-479 and Abdul Latif -Vs-Rashid Ahmed and others, reported in 2 BLC-73.
